liebermann.description_de: Cotton Claudius D II, einst ein Theil des Liber custumarum der Londoner Guildhall
liebermann.shelfmark_as_given: London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius D.ii (K2; once part of the London Guildhall’s Liber Custumarum)
liebermann.laws: Quadr, Ine, Blas, Forf, Hu, Af, AGu, App AGu, EGu, I As, As Alm, II As, Episc, Norðleod, Mirce, Að, Had, IV As, V As, III As, VI As, Ordal, I Cn, II Cn, Wl art retr, ECf retr, Lond ECf, Wl lad, CHn cor, Hn mon, Hn com, Hn, Hn Lond
liebermann.notes: Once part of the Liber custumarum of the London Guildhall, written c. 1310 with coloured decoration; one of the manuscripts of the Leges Anglorum s. XIII in Londoniis collectae: Quadripartitus laws with London inventions (ff. 2–17), Tripartita with the London interpolation (ff. 30–40), Genealogia Normannica; f. 41 (K3, 15th c.) copies Sc (Wl art retr, Wl lad, CHn cor, Hn mon, Hn com, Concordia of 1153); f. 43 Hn with CHn cor and Hn Lond. In the 17th century Harley 311 (Hn) was collated with it and Additional 16278 copied Ine to Cnut from it; Cambridge Trinity O 10, 20 used both parts.

wormald.shelfmark: London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius D.ii
wormald.wormald_origin: Used by Andrew Horn when finalizing the texts in Co and Or; bequeathed by him to the Guildhall (p. 237); reconstructed with the other Liber Custumarum pieces by Ker (p. 237 n. 304)
wormald.laws: London collection version of Quadripartitus texts (see Table 4.7 'London' column)
wormald.laws_liebermann: Quadr, Ine, Blas, Forf, Hu, Af, AGu, App AGu, EGu, I As, As Alm, II As, Episc, Norðleod, Mirce, Að, Had, IV As, V As, III As, VI As, Ordal, I Cn, II Cn, Wl art retr, ECf retr, Lond ECf, Wl lad, CHn cor, Hn mon, Hn com, Hn, Hn Lond
wormald.other_contents: One of Horn's 'presentation copies' of the London collection, larger than Textus Roffensis (pp. 252–3); calligraphic (p. 239); two columns (p. 254).
wormald.overview: An early-fourteenth-century copy of the London collection, used by the London citizen Andrew Horn when settling the texts of his other copies and left by him to the Guildhall. Wormald counts it among Horn's large calligraphic presentation copies, written in two columns.
wormald.key_quote: represent various adaptations of the 'Leges Anglorum' to the purposes of the London businessman and worthy Andrew Horn (p. 238)
wormald.guide_shelfmark: London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius D.ii (K2; once part of the London Guildhall’s Liber Custumarum)
verify_notes: Checked p. 237 (image: s xiv¹), 238–9, 252–4. Overview: 'one of the few calligraphic Quadripartitus witnesses' adjusted — Wormald says R and all the London-collection copies are calligraphic (p. 239); presentation-copy point given its source.
